citation: docs/mip/0010-api-for-other-tools.md, sections 1 and 2; proto/muster_api.proto, its header's Connecting and Versions
why: A program's first frame is a Hello naming the API and the version it speaks, and the daemon's first is a Welcome saying what it serves or a refusal saying why not. A client is written against these answers before it is written against anything else, so they are the first a newer daemon must not change. Each case is a conversation in protobuf's canonical JSON; docs/testing.md has the steps and tokens.

cases.name: a client speaking the daemon's version is welcomed with what the daemon serves
cases.why: Welcome is how a client learns which requests and topics this daemon has, down to the options of a later minor, so it asks the Welcome rather than finding out from a refusal (the header, What a client may not know yet). This is the one case that lists them, so a new request changes one line here.

cases.name: another major is refused with the daemon's version
cases.why: A client is served only by its own major, and the refusal says the daemon's version so the client can say what it needs (MIP-10, section 1).

cases.name: a version older than the oldest served is refused
cases.why: Before 1.0 a break moves the oldest version the daemon serves up to the new one, and a client older than that is refused rather than answered in a way it was not written for (the header, Versions). 0.0 is older than any version served.

cases.name: a hello naming no version is refused
cases.why: The version is what the daemon judges a client by, so a Hello without one cannot be served.

cases.name: a client newer than the daemon is welcomed and makes the check itself
cases.why: A daemon cannot know of a break made after it was built, so it serves a newer minor of its own major and says its own version; the client judges whether it can read that daemon (the header, Versions).
